slides.title: Approve [decisions] before you approve designs.
slides.lede: Each stage should resolve a business question before the next stage consumes more time and budget.

slides.title: Attractive design and [recognition] are different tests
slides.text: Only 15% of assets in the Ipsos worldwide database achieved gold status, instantly and uniquely bringing the correct brand to mind.

slides.title: Six stages, each with a [question to resolve]

items.title: Discovery and research
items.text: Are we solving the right commercial problem?

items.title: Strategic positioning
items.text: Can the firm substantiate its claimed position?

items.title: Creative direction
items.text: Does it express the brief without imitation?

items.title: Concept development
items.text: Does it work across complex corporate documents?

items.title: Application testing
items.text: Can non-design staff edit without breaking layouts?

items.title: Handover and governance
items.text: Can the practice maintain and govern it?

cards.label: Vague
cards.text: "Make it more premium" leaves the designer guessing.

cards.label: Useful
cards.text: "The type feels too informal for our acquisition reports."

slides.title: Four steps to [objective] feedback
slides.note: No design vocabulary required. **Just a reason.**

slides.title: If staff can't edit it, [handover isn't finished]
slides.text: A polished PDF proves a designer can create one. Ask your marketing owner to produce and export a real document from the template, without the designer present.

slides.title: Agree what approval means before you see a concept.
